SITUATION
A commercial greenhouse tomato operation growing vine tomatoes has seen marketable yield fall about 30% over two growing cycles, and the shortfall has repeated across successive plantings. The decline set in after a switch to a new irrigation-water source following a well upgrade. The agronomists' leading theories are under-watering or a nitrogen shortfall, so they are considering more water and feed. New leaves have looked paler than usual between the veins. Routine soil and tissue panels read broadly within range. The irrigation, fertigation, and amendment dosing are all adjustable, and dosing and amendment equipment is available. You have a limited number of experiments; you may measure quantities and apply available controls or amendments, alone or in combination. Determine what is really driving the loss and what to do about it.

OUTCOME OF INTEREST: CropYield (higher_is_better)
BUDGET: 0/15 experiments used, 15 left (code is free).
TURNS: 0/32, 32 left. Interventions so far: 0.
data files for code: (none yet)

  m0: seed treatment
  m1: wind exposure
  m2: drainage rate
  m3: crop yield
  m4: soil phosphorus
  m5: row spacing
  m6: irrigation rate
  m7: soil potassium
  m8: soil moisture
  m9: pollinator activity
  m10: night temperature
  m11: growth regulator
  m12: tissue nutrient assay

CONTROLS (ids):

  a6: set seed treatment range [0, 100]
